title: Greensleeves
description: The famous Elizabethan tune (also sung at Christmas as 'What Child Is This'), a lilting minor-key waltz with a long-short-long rhythm. A perfect introduction to 3/4 time, dotted rhythms and raised leading tones.

arrangements.label: Beginner
arrangements.notes: The verse only (pickup plus 15 bars), single-note melody over one held two-note left-hand chord per bar.
teachingPoints: Right hand starts with thumb on A4; the hand shifts down to G4 in bar 4 and up again on the pickup to the second half.
Practice the dotted-quarter/eighth rhythm (long-short) by clapping it before playing bars 2, 4 and 6.
Watch the accidentals: G# in bars 6, 7 and 14, F# in bar 14 — they are not in the key signature.
Left hand holds each two-note chord for the whole bar; change chords exactly on beat 1.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: The complete tune (verse and chorus) with a waltz-style left hand (bass note then triad) and a few right-hand thirds under the held melody notes.
teachingPoints: Left hand pattern: root on beat 1, three-note chord on beats 2-3; learn the five chord shapes (Am, C, G, Em, E) before adding the melody.
The chorus (bar 16) jumps up to G5 — prepare the hand with finger 5 during the held A4 of bar 15.
Bars 17, 19, 21 and 24 add a third below the melody (1-3 in bar 17); keep the top note louder than the harmony. In bar 22 the left-hand E chord stays below the held right-hand E4.
Hands separately at slow tempo, then together with the metronome at 72 before moving up to 100.
